locality: Anak Krakatau, Sunda Strait (between Java and Sumatra); ashfall and flight disruption affecting Banten, Lampung and wider Java/Sumatra air traffic
severity_rationale: No casualties or forced evacuations of residents have been reported, and Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency has explicitly ruled out imminent tsunami risk, which would point toward Very Low. However the scale of disruption is more than trivial: a Level III (Siaga) alert, a 3km exclusion zone, and renewed eruptive activity as recently as September 9 shut 8 airports and disrupted over 1,558 flights, stranding 270,000+ passengers at Indonesia's main international gateway. This sustained regional aviation and economic disruption, handled entirely with local/national civil aviation and disaster-mitigation resources without international assistance, is assessed as Low.
description: Anak Krakatau volcano in the Sunda Strait entered a high-level eruptive phase on September 5, 2026, sending ash plumes up to 15km (50,000 feet) high and prompting an alert Level III (Siaga) with a 3km exclusion zone for fishermen and climbers. The eruption forced closure of 8 airports including Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International, disrupting over 1,558 flights and stranding more than 270,000 passengers; Jakarta schools briefly moved to online classes. The volcano has continued to erupt intermittently through September 9-10, with Indonesia's geology agency maintaining the Siaga status while stating there is no imminent tsunami risk.

description: The Ross Fire ignited August 24, 2026 in Palo Pinto and Jack Counties, North Texas, amid extreme drought (53 days without measurable rain) and near-100°F heat, becoming the largest summertime wildfire in Texas since 2005 and the second-largest in North Texas history. As of September 9 it had burned over 90,400 acres and was 57% contained, having destroyed at least 167 structures (18 occupied homes) and damaged 95 more. Governor Abbott issued a disaster declaration and secured federal FEMA assistance; two firefighters sustained minor injuries and evacuation orders in Jack County have since been lifted, though the fire remains an active, dynamic operation.

description: Typhoon Saudel made multiple landfalls across coastal China between August 28 and September 3, 2026, prompting mass evacuations (728,000+ people across Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang and Guangdong) as it dumped extreme rainfall (400mm+ in 24 hours in Fujian's Putian). Days of subsequent flooding triggered a landslide in Suichuan County, Jiangxi on September 5 that killed 16 people across three towns (Gaoping, Zuo'an, Tanghu), with two further deaths in neighbouring Hunan province and some people still unaccounted for. Water supply contamination and infrastructure damage were reported in the worst-hit areas; more than 18,000 people were evacuated from Suichuan County alone.
